title: Phase-aware response waterfall dashboard and adaptive anomaly damping
author: Morgan Chen
description:
Background and motivation: Operators want a single, explainable surface to see where time and cost are being spent in a single invocation. Existing per-route latency panels and token-cost histograms are helpful but do not make it easy to attribute time/cost across the request lifecycle (parse -> model compute -> decode/stream). This PR introduces a phase-aware response waterfall visualization, new span phase tags, and an adaptive anomaly damping layer for alerts so that SREs get fewer noisy triggers from harmless phase skews.

What this changes: 1) New telemetry: emits span.level_phase tags (parse, queue, model, decode, stream) and numeric phase_dur_ms for all model-serving spans. Implemented lightweight phase tagging in trace_utils and serving runtime (small fast-path instrumentation to avoid added allocations). 2) Dashboard: adds observability/dashboards/response_waterfall.json (Grafana dashboard schema) with stacked-phase waterfall panels, per-tenant phase breakdown, and a selectable percentile/quantile selector. 3) Token-level correlation: enriches token-cost rollups with phase attribution to show cost-per-token by phase and by model variant. 4) Alerts: adds adaptive anomaly damping algorithm in alerts/anomaly_damping.go which decays alert sensitivity for routes where phase shifts are correlated with known model rollouts or CPU-backed rescheduling. 5) Migration: SQL migration script scripts/migrate-phase-tags.sql to backfill phase_breakdown tables for the last 30 days. 6) Tests and docs: adds e2e test to tests/e2e/response_waterfall_test.py, small unit tests for the damping policy, and runbook/docs/runbooks/phase-waterfall.md with troubleshooting steps and recommended thresholds.

Checklist: - [x] Instrumentation: minimal overhead tagging (microbench shows <1% p99 impact) - [x] Dashboard panels wired to query indices and annotated with rollout metadata - [x] Alert rules unit-tested and dogfooded on staging - [x] Migration script validated on snapshot dataset - [x] Runbook written and linked from the dashboard

How it was implemented (high-level commits): - Added phase tagging into trace emission path with a compact enum to keep tag cardinality low. - Aggregations: updated token-cost-indexer to accumulate phase_dur_ms and phase_cost_estimate. - Dashboard: built interactive waterfall with per-invocation hover showing top 3 contributing phases and approximate token cost. - Alerts: damping runs as an inline preprocessor that adjusts threshold percentile based on historical phase variance and rollout annotations.

Testing and verification: 1) Unit: added mocked span generator tests for phase tagging and aggregator. 2) Integration: response_waterfall_test replays synthetic invocations (varying queue/model/decode ratios) and asserts dashboard queries return coherent stacked sums and that alert dampening suppresses noise for predictable model rollouts. 3) Staging rollout: enabled on staging for two weeks behind a feature flag, compared alert counts to previous baseline (30% reduction in non-actionable alerts for routes with recent rollouts).

Migration and rollout plan: - Step 1: deploy instrumentation + dashboard to staging behind feature flag (0-2 days) - Step 2: run migration script on staging snapshot and validate panels (2-3 days) - Step 3: enable damping in alerts for staging traffic, monitor for under-suppression (3-7 days) - Step 4: incremental rollout to canary tenants (week 2) - Step 5: full rollout and remove feature flag (week 3)

Rollback plan: revert head branch via squash revert; disable damping preprocessor by flipping alert flag; remove dashboard from shared space if visual regressions surface.

Known limitations: backfill uses approximate mapping for older spans that do not have explicit phase markers (heuristic attribution), which can undercount parse vs queue in rare cases. We intentionally keep phase tags low-cardinality to avoid metric explosion.

Related: references ENG-3421 for alerting work and SUP-8891 (support ticket) showing noisy alerts during a recent model rollout.

Notes: performance microbench shows a 0.4% median latency increase and <1% p99; sampling rate for detailed token-phase accumulation is set to 1% by default and can be ramped per-tenant via Console.

release_notes: Add a phase-aware response waterfall dashboard (per-invocation phase breakdown) and an adaptive anomaly damping layer to reduce noisy alerts during rollouts. Includes instrumentation, backfill migration, and runbook.
testing_instructions: 1) Enable feature flag console/feature_flags/phase_waterfall.yaml for your staging tenant. 2) Run scripts/migrate-phase-tags.sql against a staging snapshot (see migration notes in docs). 3) Run tests: pytest tests/unit && pytest tests/e2e/response_waterfall_test.py. 4) Verify the Grafana dashboard under Observability -> Response Waterfall shows stacked phases and hover costs. 5) Observe alert counts for 48h to validate damping behavior.
notes: This PR was dogfooded on staging; observed ~30% reduction in non-actionable alerts for rollout-affected routes with no missed actionable alerts in the monitored window. Contact Priya for SLO tuning guidance.
